said.t: The administration is proposing an additional 20% tax on Chinese imports, which would bring the total tax to about 40%.
The administration is now using section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 as the legal basis for the new rounds of tariffs.

This is the second major batch of section 301 tariffs, after the White House announced a broad slate of tariffs on more than 80 countries in July, including the UK, Mexico and Canada, saying the countries had failed to enforce bans on forced labor.
The Yale Budget Lab estimates that tariffs currently in effect have added an additional $900 annually in costs for each US household.
An earlier Harris poll found seven in 10 Americans blamed tariffs for higher prices.

said.t: Arriving in Brussels on Thursday, the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz , reiterated his view that all EU member states should support a €45bn (£38bn) loan for Ukraine for 2027.
“When the European Union provides funding, it does so as the European Union – and that union consists of 27 member states, not 23 or 24,” he said.
“Bulgaria is going to ‌take part in the loan of 20bn [for] non-military support ​for Ukraine,” the country’s prime minister, Rumen Radev, said as he arrived at the summit.

We are ​going ​to contribute, but no money from Bulgaria for weapons.” The European Commission last week proposed a €45bn EU loan for Ukraine to fill a funding hole caused by Russia’s relentless attacks.
EU officials proposed €25bn for military spending and €20bn for Ukraine’s civilian needs, such as schools and hospitals.

EU leaders are discussing a €1.78tn proposal presented by the European Council president, António Costa, last Saturday, which represents a 10% reduction on the original €2tn plan from the European Commission.
EU leaders have struggled on Thursday to bridge divides over the bloc’s new long-term budget and agree on a $49 billion loan to help Ukraine meet its economic and military needs next year.
It’s small compared to national budgets and is financed mostly by the 27 member countries based on the size of their economies.
The 2028-2034 plan could amount to between 1% and 1.2% of gross national income, but it appears increasingly likely that the leaders might well miss an end-of-year goal to agree on it.
It would be drawn from online advertising and money that companies make from user data and could amount to 5 billion euros ($5.5 billion) a year.
The spending package foresees a 100-billion-euro ($110-billion) envelope for the government in Kyiv over seven years.
The commission again plans to raise money for the loans on capital markets, with 20 billion euros ($22 billion) earmarked for the economy and 25 billion euros ($27 billion) for the armed forces.

0df675d82a910b56.title: EU leaders struggle to agree on long-term budget, $49bn Ukraine loan
0df675d82a910b56.title_da: EU 's ledere kæmper for at blive enige om langsigtet budget, 49 mia. USD Ukraine lån

said.t: Arriving in Brussels on Thursday, the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz , reiterated his view that all EU member states should support a €45bn (£38bn) loan for Ukraine for 2027.
“When the European Union provides funding, it does so as the European Union – and that union consists of 27 member states, not 23 or 24,” he said.
“Bulgaria is going to ‌take part in the loan of 20bn [for] non-military support ​for Ukraine,” the country’s prime minister, Rumen Radev, said as he arrived at the summit.

We are ​going ​to contribute, but no money from Bulgaria for weapons.” The European Commission last week proposed a €45bn EU loan for Ukraine to fill a funding hole caused by Russia’s relentless attacks.
EU officials proposed €25bn for military spending and €20bn for Ukraine’s civilian needs, such as schools and hospitals.

EU leaders are discussing a €1.78tn proposal presented by the European Council president, António Costa, last Saturday, which represents a 10% reduction on the original €2tn plan from the European Commission.
EU leaders have struggled on Thursday to bridge divides over the bloc’s new long-term budget and agree on a $49 billion loan to help Ukraine meet its economic and military needs next year.
It’s small compared to national budgets and is financed mostly by the 27 member countries based on the size of their economies.
The 2028-2034 plan could amount to between 1% and 1.2% of gross national income, but it appears increasingly likely that the leaders might well miss an end-of-year goal to agree on it.
It would be drawn from online advertising and money that companies make from user data and could amount to 5 billion euros ($5.5 billion) a year.
The spending package foresees a 100-billion-euro ($110-billion) envelope for the government in Kyiv over seven years.
The commission again plans to raise money for the loans on capital markets, with 20 billion euros ($22 billion) earmarked for the economy and 25 billion euros ($27 billion) for the armed forces.

The law, known as Bill 21, faced legal challenges from a range of groups, including female Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers, who argued it violated their fundamental rights.

On Friday, the top court confirmed the validity of Bill 21, but ruled that the law infringes on democratic rights by banning Quebec's elected officials from wearing a face covering for religious reasons.

What to know about the Supreme Court decision on Quebec's secularism bill Civil liberty groups in Quebec have criticised Bill 21, saying it disproportionately affects Muslim women who wear the hijab, arguing that it has excluded them from key areas of public life in the province.
The National Council of Canadian Muslims (NCCM), one of the groups that challenged Bill 21, called the ruling “a dark day in our constitutional democracy”.
Quebec used it when it passed Bill 21 in 2019 and renewed it in 2024.
The Canadian Civil Liberties Association, which also challenged Bill 21, said the ruling “sends a message that even shielded laws cannot escape scrutiny entirely”.
“Bill 21 has already denied a generation of Quebecers their chosen profession in public service because of their faith.

That is discrimination, and it is why we took on this case.” Prime Minister Mark Carney told the CBC after the ruling that his colleagues in Ottawa were “carefully studying” the ruling of more than 500 pages.
Quebec passed Bill 21 in June 2019 , saying it would protect the religious neutrality of public institutions.
They said the law affected people’s “basic sense of belonging in Canadian and Quebec society”.

said.t: An explosion at a house next to a middle school in Afghanistan’s northeastern Kunar province killed at least seven students and injured 97 others Saturday.
At least six students have been killed and 97 others injured in an explosion next to a school in eastern Afghanistan’s Kunar province, according to a medical official speaking to Al Jazeera.

The explosion occurred in a house beside a middle school in the Andar Ser area of Kunar province, eastern Afghanistan, at about 10am (05:30 GMT) on Saturday, Mawlawi Sami-ul-Haq, the director of Information and Culture in Kunar, told Al Jazeera separately.
In August, a hand grenade attack at a school complex in the Afghan capital of Kabul wounded more than 40 children aged between nine and 14.

Farid Dehqan, spokesperson for the Kunar Provincial Police Headquarters, said the explosion occurred at 10 a.m. at a school in the province's Andar Ser area, adding that several students were killed or wounded in the blast.

said.t: Russia and Ukraine exchanged drone strikes Saturday, killing at least two people and injuring 20 others, officials on both sides said.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said its air defenses intercepted and destroyed 1,246 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones overnight.
Ukraine’s air force said Russia launched 162 attack drones, of which 141 were shot down or suppressed.

Russian forces carried out more than 20 drone attacks across four districts in Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk region, wounding five people, including a child, regional military administration chief Oleksandr Hanzha said on Telegram.
It said the targets included an electrical substation in Bila Tserkva, a fuel tank in Kiliya in the Odesa region and four locomotives in the Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr and Kharkiv regions.
Russian forces have attacked Ukraine with 155 attack drones of various types and Parodiya decoy UAVs since the evening of 26 November.
A total of 110 drones have been destroyed, although some hits have been recorded.
Source: Ukraine's Air Force Quote: "As of 08:00, [Ukrainian] air defence forces had destroyed or jammed 110 Shahed (51 jet-powered), Gerbera and other types of drones.

According to the military, from 18:00 on Thursday, 26 November, Russian invaders deployed 155 Shahed-type strike drones (83 of which were jet-powered), ‘Herbera’ drones and ‘Parody’-type decoy drones to attack Ukraine.

Preliminary figures indicate that, as of 08:00 on Friday, air defences had shot down or jammed 110 Russian Shahed-type drones (51 of which were jet-powered), ‘Herbera’ drones and other types of drones.
Air strikes by the invaders were recorded at 27 locations, whilst the wreckage of downed targets was found at a further four.

In brief: Russia launched 155 drones against Ukraine overnight on Friday, Nov.
27, striking infrastructure in several regions and disrupting electricity supplies.
Russia launched 155 attack drones against Ukraine overnight on Friday, Nov.

27, targeting energy, railway and other critical infrastructure across several regions, while Estonia scrambled NATO fighter jets after issuing a temporary air threat warning over possible drone activity.
The attack included 83 jet-powered Shahed drones.
As of Friday morning, Ukrainian air defenses had intercepted or suppressed 110 drones, including 51 jet-powered Shaheds.
Ukraine’s Energy Ministry reported power outages in the Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kirovohrad, Sumy, Kharkiv and Kherson regions across central and southern Ukraine.
